https://openai.com/index/procgen-minerl-.summary: We’re excited to announce that OpenAI is co-organizing two NeurIPS 2020 competitions with AIcrowd, Carnegie Mellon University, and DeepMind, using Procgen Benchmark and MineRL.

https://openai.com/index/image-gpt.title: Image GPT
https://openai.com/index/image-gpt.summary: We find that, just as a large transformer model trained on language can generate coherent text, the same exact model trained on pixel sequences can generate coherent image completions and samples. By establishing a correlation between sample quality and image classification accuracy, we show that our best generative model also contains features competitive with top convolutional nets in the unsupervised setting.

https://openai.com/index/openai-api.title: OpenAI API
https://openai.com/index/openai-api.summary: We’re releasing an API for accessing new AI models developed by OpenAI.

https://openai.com/index/ai-and-efficien.title: AI and efficiency
https://openai.com/index/ai-and-efficien.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012 the amount of compute needed to train a neural net to the same performance on ImageNet classification has been decreasing by a factor of 2 every 16 months. Compared to 2012, it now takes 44 times less compute to train a neural network to the level of AlexNet (by contrast, Moore’s Law would yield an 11x cost improvement over this period). Our results suggest that for AI tasks with high levels of recent investment, algorithmic progress has yielded more gains than classical hardware efficiency.

https://openai.com/index/jukebox.title: Jukebox
https://openai.com/index/jukebox.summary: We’re introducing Jukebox, a neural net that generates music, including rudimentary singing, as raw audio in a variety of genres and artist styles. We’re releasing the model weights and code, along with a tool to explore the generated samples.

https://openai.com/index/improving-verif.title: Improving verifiability in AI development
https://openai.com/index/improving-verif.summary: We’ve contributed to a multi-stakeholder report by 58 co-authors at 30 organizations, including the Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Mila, Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society, Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, and Center for Security and Emerging Technologies. This report describes 10 mechanisms to improve the verifiability of claims made about AI systems. Developers can use these tools to provide evidence that AI systems are safe, secure, fair, or privacy-preserving. Users, policymakers, and civil society can use these tools to evaluate AI development processes.

https://openai.com/index/microscope.title: OpenAI Microscope
https://openai.com/index/microscope.summary: We’re introducing OpenAI Microscope, a collection of visualizations of every significant layer and neuron of eight vision “model organisms” which are often studied in interpretability. Microscope makes it easier to analyze the features that form inside these neural networks, and we hope it will help the research community as we move towards understanding these complicated systems.

https://openai.com/index/openai-pytorch.title: OpenAI standardizes on PyTorch
https://openai.com/index/openai-pytorch.summary: We are standardizing OpenAI’s deep learning framework on PyTorch.

https://openai.com/index/scaling-laws-fo.title: Scaling laws for neural language models

https://openai.com/index/dota-2-with-lar.title: Dota 2 with large scale deep reinforcement learning

https://openai.com/index/deep-double-des.title: Deep double descent
https://openai.com/index/deep-double-des.summary: We show that the double descent phenomenon occurs in CNNs, ResNets, and transformers: performance first improves, then gets worse, and then improves again with increasing model size, data size, or training time. This effect is often avoided through careful regularization. While this behavior appears to be fairly universal, we don’t yet fully understand why it happens, and view further study of this phenomenon as an important research direction.

https://openai.com/index/procgen-benchma.title: Procgen Benchmark
https://openai.com/index/procgen-benchma.summary: We’re releasing Procgen Benchmark, 16 simple-to-use procedurally-generated environments which provide a direct measure of how quickly a reinforcement learning agent learns generalizable skills.

https://openai.com/index/benchmarking-sa.title: Benchmarking safe exploration in deep reinforcement learning

https://openai.com/index/safety-gym.title: Safety Gym
https://openai.com/index/safety-gym.summary: We’re releasing Safety Gym, a suite of environments and tools for measuring progress towards reinforcement learning agents that respect safety constraints while training.

https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-1-5b-rele.title: GPT-2: 1.5B release
https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-1-5b-rele.summary: As the final model release of GPT-2’s staged release, we’re releasing the largest version (1.5B parameters) of GPT-2 along with code and model weights to facilitate detection of outputs of GPT-2 models. While there have been larger language models released since August, we’ve continued with our original staged release plan in order to provide the community with a test case of a full staged release process. We hope that this test case will be useful to developers of future powerful models, and we’re actively continuing the conversation with the AI community on responsible publication.

https://openai.com/index/solving-rubiks-.title: Solving Rubik’s Cube with a robot hand
https://openai.com/index/solving-rubiks-.summary: We’ve trained a pair of neural networks to solve the Rubik’s Cube with a human-like robot hand. The neural networks are trained entirely in simulation, using the same reinforcement learning code as OpenAI Five paired with a new technique called Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR). The system can handle situations it never saw during training, such as being prodded by a stuffed giraffe. This shows that reinforcement learning isn’t just a tool for virtual tasks, but can solve physical-world problems requiring unprecedented dexterity.

https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.title: OpenAI Scholars 2020: Applications open
https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.summary: We are now accepting applications for our third class of OpenAI Scholars.

https://openai.com/index/fine-tuning-gpt.title: Fine-tuning GPT-2 from human preferences
https://openai.com/index/fine-tuning-gpt.summary: We’ve fine-tuned the 774M parameter GPT-2 language model using human feedback for various tasks, successfully matching the preferences of the external human labelers, though those preferences did not always match our own. Specifically, for summarization tasks the labelers preferred sentences copied wholesale from the input (we’d only asked them to ensure accuracy), so our models learned to copy. Summarization required 60k human labels; simpler tasks which continue text in various styles required only 5k. Our motivation is to move safety techniques closer to the general task of “machines talking to humans,” which we believe is key to extracting information about human values.

https://openai.com/index/emergent-tool-u.title: Emergent tool use from multi-agent interaction
https://openai.com/index/emergent-tool-u.summary: We’ve observed agents discovering progressively more complex tool use while playing a simple game of hide-and-seek. Through training in our new simulated hide-and-seek environment, agents build a series of six distinct strategies and counterstrategies, some of which we did not know our environment supported. The self-supervised emergent complexity in this simple environment further suggests that multi-agent co-adaptation may one day produce extremely complex and intelligent behavior.

https://openai.com/index/testing-robustn.title: Testing robustness against unforeseen adversaries
https://openai.com/index/testing-robustn.summary: We’ve developed a method to assess whether a neural network classifier can reliably defend against adversarial attacks not seen during training. Our method yields a new metric, UAR (Unforeseen Attack Robustness), which evaluates the robustness of a single model against an unanticipated attack, and highlights the need to measure performance across a more diverse range of unforeseen attacks.

https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-6-month-f.title: GPT-2: 6-month follow-up
https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-6-month-f.summary: We’re releasing the 774 million parameter GPT-2 language model after the release of our small 124M model in February, staged release of our medium 355M model in May, and subsequent research with partners and the AI community into the model’s potential for misuse and societal benefit. We’re also releasing an open-source legal agreement to make it easier for organizations to initiate model-sharing partnerships with each other, and are publishing a technical report about our experience in coordinating with the wider AI research community on publication norms.

https://openai.com/index/learning-day.title: Learning Day
https://openai.com/index/learning-day.summary: At OpenAI, each Thursday is Learning Day: a day where employees have the option to self-study technical skills that will make them better at their job but which aren’t being learned from daily work.

https://openai.com/index/microsoft-inves.title: Microsoft invests in and partners with OpenAI to support us building beneficial AGI
https://openai.com/index/microsoft-inves.summary: Microsoft is investing $1 billion in OpenAI to support us building artificial general intelligence (AGI) with widely distributed economic benefits. We’re partnering to develop a hardware and software platform within Microsoft Azure which will scale to AGI. We’ll jointly develop new Azure AI supercomputing technologies, and Microsoft will become our exclusive cloud provider—so we’ll be working hard together to further extend Microsoft Azure’s capabilities in large-scale AI systems.

https://openai.com/index/cooperation-on-.title: Why responsible AI development needs cooperation on safety
https://openai.com/index/cooperation-on-.summary: We’ve written a policy research paper identifying four strategies that can be used today to improve the likelihood of long-term industry cooperation on safety norms in AI: communicating risks and benefits, technical collaboration, increased transparency, and incentivizing standards. Our analysis shows that industry cooperation on safety will be instrumental in ensuring that AI systems are safe and beneficial, but competitive pressures could lead to a collective action problem, potentially causing AI companies to under-invest in safety. We hope these strategies will encourage greater cooperation on the safe development of AI and lead to better global outcomes of AI.

https://openai.com/index/symposium-2019.summary: We hosted the first OpenAI Robotics Symposium on April 27, 2019.

https://openai.com/index/openai-fellows-.summary: Our second class of OpenAI Fellows has wrapped up, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship. https://openai.com/index/transfer-of-adv.title: Transfer of adversarial robustness between perturbation types

https://openai.com/index/musenet.title: MuseNet
https://openai.com/index/musenet.summary: We’ve created MuseNet, a deep neural network that can generate 4-minute musical compositions with 10 different instruments, and can combine styles from country to Mozart to the Beatles. MuseNet was not explicitly programmed with our understanding of music, but instead discovered patterns of harmony, rhythm, and style by learning to predict the next token in hundreds of thousands of MIDI files. MuseNet uses the same general-purpose unsupervised technology as GPT-2, a large-scale transformer model trained to predict the next token in a sequence, whether audio or text.

https://openai.com/index/sparse-transfor.title: Generative modeling with sparse transformers
https://openai.com/index/sparse-transfor.summary: We’ve developed the Sparse Transformer, a deep neural network which sets new records at predicting what comes next in a sequence—whether text, images, or sound. It uses an algorithmic improvement of the attention mechanism to extract patterns from sequences 30x longer than possible previously.

https://openai.com/index/openai-five-def.title: OpenAI Five defeats Dota 2 world champions
https://openai.com/index/openai-five-def.summary: OpenAI Five is the first AI to beat the world champions in an esports game, having won two back-to-back games versus the world champion Dota 2 team, OG, at Finals this weekend. Both OpenAI Five and DeepMind’s AlphaStar had previously beaten good pros privately but lost their live pro matches, making this also the first time an AI has beaten esports pros on livestream.

https://openai.com/index/openai-five-fin.title: OpenAI Five Finals
https://openai.com/index/openai-five-fin.summary: We’ll be holding our final live event for OpenAI Five at 11:30am PT on April 13.

https://openai.com/index/energy-based-mo.title: Implicit generation and generalization methods for energy-based models
https://openai.com/index/energy-based-mo.summary: We’ve made progress towards stable and scalable training of energy-based models (EBMs) resulting in better sample quality and generalization ability than existing models. Generation in EBMs spends more compute to continually refine its answers and doing so can generate samples competitive with GANs at low temperatures, while also having mode coverage guarantees of likelihood-based models. We hope these findings stimulate further research into this promising class of models.

https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Meet our Scholars
https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.summary: Our class of eight scholars (out of 550 applicants) brings together collective expertise in literature, philosophy, cell biology, statistics, economics, quantum physics, and business innovation.

https://openai.com/index/openai-lp.title: OpenAI LP
https://openai.com/index/openai-lp.summary: We’ve created OpenAI LP, a new “capped-profit” company that allows us to rapidly increase our investments in compute and talent while including checks and balances to actualize our mission.

https://openai.com/index/introducing-act.title: Introducing Activation Atlases
https://openai.com/index/introducing-act.summary: We’ve created activation atlases (in collaboration with Google researchers), a new technique for visualizing what interactions between neurons can represent. As AI systems are deployed in increasingly sensitive contexts, having a better understanding of their internal decision-making processes will let us identify weaknesses and investigate failures.

https://openai.com/index/neural-mmo.title: Neural MMO: A massively multiagent game environment
https://openai.com/index/neural-mmo.summary: We’re releasing a Neural MMO, a massively multiagent game environment for reinforcement learning agents. Our platform supports a large, variable number of agents within a persistent and open-ended task. The inclusion of many agents and species leads to better exploration, divergent niche formation, and greater overall competence.

https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL: Workshop review
https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-.summary: On February 2, we held our first Spinning Up Workshop as part of our new education initiative at OpenAI.

https://openai.com/index/ai-safety-needs.title: AI safety needs social scientists
https://openai.com/index/ai-safety-needs.summary: We’ve written a paper arguing that long-term AI safety research needs social scientists to ensure AI alignment algorithms succeed when actual humans are involved. Properly aligning advanced AI systems with human values requires resolving many uncertainties related to the psychology of human rationality, emotion, and biases. The aim of this paper is to spark further collaboration between machine learning and social science researchers, and we plan to hire social scientists to work on this full time at OpenAI.

https://openai.com/index/better-language.title: Better language models and their implications
https://openai.com/index/better-language.summary: We’ve trained a large-scale unsupervised language model which generates coherent paragraphs of text, achieves state-of-the-art performance on many language modeling benchmarks, and performs rudimentary reading comprehension, machine translation, question answering, and summarization—all without task-specific training.

https://openai.com/index/computational-l.title: Computational limitations in robust classification and win-win results

https://openai.com/index/openai-summer-f.title: OpenAI Fellows Summer 2018: Final projects
https://openai.com/index/openai-summer-f.summary: Our first cohort of OpenAI Fellows has concluded, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship.

https://openai.com/index/how-ai-training.title: How AI training scales
https://openai.com/index/how-ai-training.summary: We’ve discovered that the gradient noise scale, a simple statistical metric, predicts the parallelizability of neural network training on a wide range of tasks. Since complex tasks tend to have noisier gradients, increasingly large batch sizes are likely to become useful in the future, removing one potential limit to further growth of AI systems. More broadly, these results show that neural network training need not be considered a mysterious art, but can be rigorized and systematized.

https://openai.com/index/quantifying-gen.title: Quantifying generalization in reinforcement learning
https://openai.com/index/quantifying-gen.summary: We’re releasing CoinRun, a training environment which provides a metric for an agent’s ability to transfer its experience to novel situations and has already helped clarify a longstanding puzzle in reinforcement learning. CoinRun strikes a desirable balance in complexity: the environment is simpler than traditional platformer games like Sonic the Hedgehog but still poses a worthy generalization challenge for state of the art algorithms.

https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL
https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-.summary: We’re releasing Spinning Up in Deep RL, an educational resource designed to let anyone learn to become a skilled practitioner in deep reinforcement learning. Spinning Up consists of crystal-clear examples of RL code, educational exercises, documentation, and tutorials.

https://openai.com/index/learning-concep.title: Learning concepts with energy functions
https://openai.com/index/learning-concep.summary: We’ve developed an energy-based model that can quickly learn to identify and generate instances of concepts, such as near, above, between, closest, and furthest, expressed as sets of 2d points. Our model learns these concepts after only five demonstrations. We also show cross-domain transfer: we use concepts learned in a 2d particle environment to solve tasks on a 3-dimensional physics-based robot.

https://openai.com/index/plan-online-lea.title: Plan online, learn offline: Efficient learning and exploration via model-based control

https://openai.com/index/reinforcement-l.title: Reinforcement learning with prediction-based rewards
https://openai.com/index/reinforcement-l.summary: We’ve developed Random Network Distillation (RND), a prediction-based method for encouraging reinforcement learning agents to explore their environments through curiosity, which for the first time exceeds average human performance on Montezuma’s Revenge.

https://openai.com/index/learning-comple.title: Learning complex goals with iterated amplification
https://openai.com/index/learning-comple.summary: We’re proposing an AI safety technique called iterated amplification that lets us specify complicated behaviors and goals that are beyond human scale, by demonstrating how to decompose a task into simpler sub-tasks, rather than by providing labeled data or a reward function. Although this idea is in its very early stages and we have only completed experiments on simple toy algorithmic domains, we’ve decided to present it in its preliminary state because we think it could prove to be a scalable approach to AI safety.

https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Applications open
https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.summary: We are now accepting applications for our second cohort of OpenAI Scholars, a program where we provide 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.

https://openai.com/index/openai-fellows-.summary: We are now accepting applications for OpenAI Fellows and Interns for 2019.

https://openai.com/index/the-internation.summary: OpenAI Five lost two games against top Dota 2 players at The International in Vancouver this week, maintaining a good chance of winning for the first 20–35 minutes of both games.

https://openai.com/index/openai-five-ben.title: OpenAI Five Benchmark: Results
https://openai.com/index/openai-five-ben.summary: Yesterday, OpenAI Five won a best-of-three against a team of 99.95th percentile Dota players: Blitz, Cap, Fogged, Merlini, and MoonMeander—four of whom have played Dota professionally—in front of a live audience and 100,000 concurrent livestream viewers.

https://openai.com/index/learning-dexter.title: Learning dexterity
https://openai.com/index/learning-dexter.summary: We’ve trained a human-like robot hand to manipulate physical objects with unprecedented dexterity.

https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.title: OpenAI Scholars 2018: Meet our Scholars
https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.summary: Our first class of OpenAI Scholars is underway, and you can now follow along as this group of experienced software developers becomes machine learning practitioners.

https://openai.com/index/openai-five-ben.title: OpenAI Five Benchmark
https://openai.com/index/openai-five-ben.summary: The OpenAI Five Benchmark match is now over!

https://openai.com/index/glow.title: Glow: Better reversible generative models
https://openai.com/index/glow.summary: We introduce Glow, a reversible generative model which uses invertible 1x1 convolutions. It extends previous work on reversible generative models and simplifies the architecture. Our model can generate realistic high resolution images, supports efficient sampling, and discovers features that can be used to manipulate attributes of data. We’re releasing code for the model and an online visualization tool so people can explore and build on these results.

https://openai.com/index/learning-montez.title: Learning Montezuma’s Revenge from a single demonstration
https://openai.com/index/learning-montez.summary: We’ve trained an agent to achieve a high score of 74,500 on Montezuma’s Revenge from a single human demonstration, better than any previously published result. Our algorithm is simple: the agent plays a sequence of games starting from carefully chosen states from the demonstration, and learns from them by optimizing the game score using PPO, the same reinforcement learning algorithm that underpins OpenAI Five.

https://openai.com/index/openai-five.title: OpenAI Five
https://openai.com/index/openai-five.summary: Our team of five neural networks, OpenAI Five, has started to defeat amateur human teams at Dota 2.

https://openai.com/index/retro-contest-r.title: Retro Contest: Results
https://openai.com/index/retro-contest-r.summary: The first run of our Retro Contest—exploring the development of algorithms that can generalize from previous experience—is now complete.

https://openai.com/index/learning-policy.title: Learning policy representations in multiagent systems

https://openai.com/index/language-unsupe.title: Improving language understanding with unsupervised learning
https://openai.com/index/language-unsupe.summary: We’ve obtained state-of-the-art results on a suite of diverse language tasks with a scalable, task-agnostic system, which we’re also releasing. Our approach is a combination of two existing ideas: transformers and unsupervised pre-training. These results provide a convincing example that pairing supervised learning methods with unsupervised pre-training works very well; this is an idea that many have explored in the past, and we hope our result motivates further research into applying this idea on larger and more diverse datasets.

https://openai.com/index/gamepad.title: GamePad: A learning environment for theorem proving

https://openai.com/index/openai-fellows.title: OpenAI Fellows Fall 2018
https://openai.com/index/openai-fellows.summary: We’re now accepting applications for the next cohort of OpenAI Fellows, a program which offers a compensated 6-month apprenticeship in AI research at OpenAI.

https://openai.com/index/gym-retro.title: Gym Retro
https://openai.com/index/gym-retro.summary: We’re releasing the full version of Gym Retro, a platform for reinforcement learning research on games. This brings our publicly-released game count from around 70 Atari games and 30 Sega games to over 1,000 games across a variety of backing emulators. We’re also releasing the tool we use to add new games to the platform.

https://openai.com/index/ai-and-compute.title: AI and compute
https://openai.com/index/ai-and-compute.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore’s Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it’s worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today’s capabilities.

https://openai.com/index/debate.title: AI safety via debate
https://openai.com/index/debate.summary: We’re proposing an AI safety technique which trains agents to debate topics with one another, using a human to judge who wins.

https://openai.com/index/evolved-policy-.title: Evolved Policy Gradients
https://openai.com/index/evolved-policy-.summary: We’re releasing an experimental metalearning approach called Evolved Policy Gradients, a method that evolves the loss function of learning agents, which can enable fast training on novel tasks. Agents trained with EPG can succeed at basic tasks at test time that were outside their training regime, like learning to navigate to an object on a different side of the room from where it was placed during training.

https://openai.com/index/gotta-learn-fas.title: Gotta Learn Fast: A new benchmark for generalization in RL

https://openai.com/index/reptile.title: Reptile: A scalable meta-learning algorithm
https://openai.com/index/reptile.summary: We’ve developed a simple meta-learning algorithm called Reptile which works by repeatedly sampling a task, performing stochastic gradient descent on it, and updating the initial parameters towards the final parameters learned on that task. Reptile is the application of the Shortest Descent algorithm to the meta-learning setting, and is mathematically similar to first-order MAML (which is a version of the well-known MAML algorithm) that only needs black-box access to an optimizer such as SGD or Adam, with similar computational efficiency and performance.

https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.title: OpenAI Scholars
https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars.summary: We’re providing 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.

https://openai.com/index/multi-goal-rein.title: Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning: Challenging robotics environments and request for research

https://openai.com/index/ingredients-for.title: Ingredients for robotics research
https://openai.com/index/ingredients-for.summary: We’re releasing eight simulated robotics environments and a Baselines implementation of Hindsight Experience Replay, all developed for our research over the past year. We’ve used these environments to train models which work on physical robots. We’re also releasing a set of requests for robotics research.

https://openai.com/index/openai-hackatho.title: OpenAI hackathon
https://openai.com/index/openai-hackatho.summary: Come to OpenAI’s office in San Francisco’s Mission District for talks and a hackathon on Saturday, March 3rd.

https://openai.com/index/preparing-for-m.title: Preparing for malicious uses of AI
https://openai.com/index/preparing-for-m.summary: We’ve co-authored a paper that forecasts how malicious actors could misuse AI technology, and potential ways we can prevent and mitigate these threats. This paper is the outcome of almost a year of sustained work with our colleagues at the Future of Humanity Institute, the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, the Center for a New American Security, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and others.

https://openai.com/index/openai-supporte.title: OpenAI supporters

https://www.anthropic.com/news/christoph.title: Physicist Christopher Stubbs joins Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust
https://www.anthropic.com/news/christoph.summary: Dr. Christopher Stubbs, an experimental physicist and former Dean of Science at Harvard University, has joined Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust. He brings to the Trust decades of scientific expertise across observational cosmology and precision measurement. He has also advised the US government on national security and arms control.  “I am honored to join Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust and to help the company deliver on its public benefit mission,” said Stubbs. “I use AI tools in my research every day and see what they make possible, and as an educator I have confronted some of the hard questions they raise. As a grandfather, I want to help ensure that AI is developed and deployed for the long-term benefit of humanity.” Stubbs is the Samuel C. Moncher Professor of Physics and of Astronomy at Harvard, where he served as Dean of Science from 2018 to 2024. In 1998, as a member of the High-Z Supernova Search Team, he helped discover the accelerating expansion of the universe, work that later earned the team the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. He was also the inaugural project scientist for what is now the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which started a 10-year survey of the southern sky in June. One of its aims is to study the accelerating expansion he helped discover. More recently, he’s written about how to keep AI-assisted research reproducible when models can give different answers to the same question. He’s a member of JASON, an independent group of scientists who have advised the US government on defense and technology since 1960. "When Chris found evidence that the universe was expanding at a rate no one expected, he and his team followed the data even when it went against the prevailing wisdom of the field. As AI starts to transform how science itself is done, Chris’s intellectual honesty, rigor, and commitment to the truth are the values we want shaping the future of this technology, and I’m grateful he’s bringing his deep expertise to the Trust," said Daniela Amodei, Co-founder and President of Anthropic. Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation, which means we’re structured to balance commercial growth with our public benefit purpose. The Trust exists to help us hold that balance over the long term. It has the authority to appoint a majority of Anthropic’s board, and Trustees advise the board and our leadership on critical decisions, particularly those involving risks and societal impacts of AI.  This week we published our first Public Benefit Report [link], a public account of how we’re working toward our mission and where we’re falling short. The Trustees helped define the five mission pillars it measures us against, and the report closes with their assessment of our progress to date. Subject to stockholder approval, we’ve also committed to setting aside a portion of Anthropic’s shares to Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows.  “Anthropic's Public Benefit Report sets out what we’re all working toward: helping the world build powerful AI safely, and making sure the technology drives advances that meaningfully improve people’s lives and society as a whole,” added Neil Buddy Shah, Chair of the Long-Term Benefit Trust. “Both goals depend on a deep understanding of frontier science and leading with integrity. Not only has Chris worked on some of the hardest problems in science, but he has consistently been a high-integrity leader of large, complex, collaborative scientific endeavors across academia, government, and the national laboratories. That will be of great value to the Trust as we support Anthropic in developing AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.” Stubbs, the Trust’s first physicist, joins Shah, national security expert Richard Fontaine, and former Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke. Trustees are independent of the company’s management and investors.
